verdict.rationale: Kick documents period locking: once the accountant closes a period and locks it, the finalized books are protected from changes by anyone, and reports for locked periods stay accurate and stable. Non-financial actions such as notes and receipts remain allowed. missing for 10: documented unlock/reopen workflow and who can perform it, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an accountant, I can lock closed periods so prior-period numbers cannot change without an explicit reopening

citations.quote: When your accountant finishes reviewing and closing a period, they lock it. A lock protects the finalized books for that period from being changed - by anyone, including you.
Reports for locked periods remain accurate and stable.
Once a period is locked, you can still: View all transactions and reports for that period, Upload and attach receipts, Add notes to transactions
